# heo cheatsheet: people

For a person at a terminal. Start with [getting started](manual/getting-started.md); every verb is
explained in [commands](manual/commands.md), and the full table of effects and roles is the [command
reference](manual/command-reference.md).

## First hour

```sh
heo service setup api              # enable REST on loopback and mint the surface token
heo service start                  # run the daemon in the foreground
heo service status                 # in another terminal: is everything ready
heo channel list                   # configured connections
heo conversation list --status open
heo message list --conversation conv_123
heo message reply conv_123 --text "Thanks, we're on it." --dry-run
heo delivery get op_123            # did the reply leave
heo service stop                   # drain and exit
```

## Reading the tables

Effect: `read` changes nothing; `write` changes uma or the profile; `write-shared` also reaches a
provider or the daemon; `destructive-*` cannot be undone and asks to be confirmed. Roles: `operator`
configures, `desk` works conversations, `viewer` reads, `external` reads public content only. Every
write takes `--dry-run`, `--idempotency-key` and, where it is optimistic, `--revision`.

To react to events with your own program in any language, see [write a
plugin](manual/hooks.md#write-a-plugin-in-any-language); `heo hook` runs, tests and replays plugins.
